title: Postman environment export: literal value in a variable typed secret
summary: A synthetic Postman environment export: an id, a name and a values array of {key, value, type, enabled} entries. One entry is an ordinary variable (a base URL on an example host). The other is named postman_api_key, has type secret and holds a synthetic PMAK-shaped literal in its value property.
rationale: The word secret appears on the entry, and Postman documents that its application masks or encrypts a secret variable. That is a statement about the application, not about the exported bytes, and the sources read here do not say whether an export omits, masks or keeps the value. If the literal is in the file it is in the file: a reader that treats type secret as meaning the value is already protected misses it, and one that treats the whole entry as the secret over-reports the label, the type and the enabled flag. The span is the credential string only.

expectation.rationale: Flag one span: the PMAK-shaped string in the value property of the secret-typed entry, on the family grammar (two artifacts by different maintainers are consistent with PMAK- followed by 24 hex, a hyphen and 34 hex). The export structure comes from Postman's SDK documentation of the environment and globals data structure. This input is a synthetic stress case derived from that structure; it is not an observed export, and nothing here establishes that Postman writes secret-typed values into an exported file. Preconditions: exported JSON text read as UTF-8 with no decoding or variable resolution assumed.

sources.supports: The postman-api-token rule matches PMAK- followed by 24 hexadecimal characters, a hyphen and 34 hexadecimal characters.
The Postman detector pattern matches PMAK- followed by 59 characters, consistent with the 24 + hyphen + 34 split but wider in alphabet.
Environment and globals are exported and imported as a data structure with a name and a values array of variable definitions with a key and a value.
A variable definition may carry type, secret and disabled properties; the documented example of a secret variable has type secret.
A global, environment or collection variable can be set as secure, which encrypts the value in Postman; secure variables are stored locally and are not shared with the team.

Historical, snapshot of 2025-06-02: a secret type masks the initial and current values for all workspace members; the current page no longer describes initial and current values and says values are local by default.
sources.locator: sections: Initial and current values; Variable types (snapshot 20250602171032)

sources.supports: Environments can be exported as JSON files that can be imported into any Postman instance, shared with others or used with the Postman CLI.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04; no scanner was run. Origin: synthetic stress derived from the SDK data-structure description. Unresolved, not recorded as a claim: whether an exported environment contains the value of a secret-typed variable (the export page does not say). A real export is not available to this repository and none was fetched or logged into.
